questions.question: What is meant by AIDA model? How is it beneficial in advertising ? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by AIDA model? How is it beneficial in advertising?
  • AIDA Model
  • AIDA Model is a selling concept presented by Elmo Lewis to explain how
  • personal selling works. AIDA Model outlines the processes for achieving
  • promotional goals in terms of stages of consumer involvement with the message.
  • The Stages are Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action.
  • Benefits: AIDA helps in creating more effective messages. By focusing on
  • attention-grabbing elements, maintaining interest, building desire, and providing
  • a clear call-to-action, businesses can craft messages that resonate with their
  • audience.

questions.question: Discuss how advertisers use the three component model of attitudes to prepare advertising campaigns. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss how advertisers use the three component model of
  • attitudes to prepare advertising campaigns.
  • The Three Components of Attitudes
  • A) Cognitive component (Beliefs / Knowledge)- This includes what the person
  • thinks is true about the object (facts, perceptions, and learned
  • information).
  • B) Affective component (Feelings / Emotions) - This includes emotional
  • reactions, likes/dislikes, and mood-linked responses.
  • C) Conative component (Behavioural intention / tendency) - This reflects the
  • intention or likelihood of acting.
  • Advertising often targets these three components differently:
  • • Cognitive persuasion: providing reasons and evidence (features, comparisons,
  • proof).
  • • Affective persuasion: building positive emotions around the brand (music,
  • warmth, humour, aesthetic).
  • • Conative persuasion: triggering intention/action (discounts, call-to-action, trial
  • offers).

questions.question: Explain the concepts of Unconditioned Stimulus (US) and Unconditioned Response (UR) in classical conditioning. Illustrate the mechanism with two advertising examples. / [CO1] [10x4 = 40]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concepts of Unconditioned Stimulus (US)
  • and Unconditioned Response (UR) in classical
  • conditioning. Illustrate the mechanism with two
  • advertising examples.
  • Classical conditioning in advertising works by pairing a
  • product (neutral stimulus) with positive imagery, music, or
  • emotions (unconditioned stimulus) to create a positive,
  • automatic association (conditioned response) in the
  • consumer's mind. It uses repetition and consistent pairing to
  • foster brand recognition, preference, and loyalty.
  • Examples:
  • Coca-Cola and Happiness: Coca-Cola pairs its beverage
  • with images of smiling friends, music, and sunny beach
  • settings. The warmth of summer (unconditioned stimulus)
  • paired with the drink creates an automatic positive feeling
  • (unconditioned response), leading consumers to associate
  • Coke with joy.
  • Celebrity Endorsements: Linking a product with a beloved
  • celebrity (unconditioned stimulus) transfers the public's
  • admiration for that person to the brand. For example, a sports
  • star paired with a soft drink brand.
